subject.title: fix: unify macos dashboard auth startup

question: Should the macOS embedded Dashboard browser receive native/stored device tokens, or only configured shared token/password credentials?
rationale: This PR fixes fast-path parity by extending native-token resolution into browser injection, while the linked sibling issue and PR argue that native device tokens must stay out of the browser Control UI auth surface.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Rework this branch or close it in favor of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98488 so the embedded Dashboard injects only configured shared token/password credentials while preserving current-main endpoint observation.

options.title: Allow native-token browser parity
options.body: Keep this PR direction only if maintainers explicitly accept native/stored operator tokens as valid browser Dashboard auth and require security review plus macOS proof before merge.

options.title: Pause both drafts
options.body: Hold both open drafts until a macOS owner documents the intended Dashboard browser-auth boundary and chooses one implementation path.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Rework this branch or close it in favor of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98488 so the embedded Dashboard injects only configured shared token/password credentials while preserving current-main endpoint observation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently maintained the central Dashboard window and endpoint-following code touched by the conflicting auth paths.
